results.title: SurgePix vs Gamma (2026): The Editable AI PPT Alternative | SurgePix
results.content:
SurgePix is built around that exact moment: generate a visual, then edit every layer — no re-rolling. Here's an honest head-to-head so you can pick the right one. (New to AI decks? Start with our complete guide to making a presentation with AI. Want the whole field, not just these two? See our comparison of the best AI PPT tools in 2026.)

## TL;DR — which should you pick?

 Pick Gamma if you want the fastest possible first draft and mostly keep what it gives you.
 Pick SurgePix if you want to keep editing after generation — change text, inpaint one area, restyle a single element, and export a real, still-editable `.pptx` — and make more than slides (images, carousels, posters) from one workspace. [...] Things a slides-only tool simply can't do: redraw just the area you select (inpaint), edit text that's baked into an image, crop, remove a background in one click, and @mention any element to reference or restyle it. Your deck and its visuals get finished in one place.

Brush-based inpainting. SurgePix lets you paint over just a part of an image and describe the change — say, recolor a person's shirt — without splitting the image apart first. Gamma can only swap or edit a whole image block; it has no way to repaint a region inside an image.(Full guide: how to edit part of an AI image.)

### 4. A real .pptx — still editable [...] You keep re-generating to fix one small thing.
 You need to edit text or objects inside an image, not just on a slide.
 You want a `.pptx` you can actually edit afterward.
 You make images and social visuals too, not only decks.
 You want AI design callable from Claude Code or Cursor.

→ Try SurgePix free — generate a deck, then edit every layer.

## FAQ

### Is SurgePix a good Gamma alternative?

Yes, if your priority is editing after generation and multi-format output. Gamma is still great for the fastest first draft.

results.title: 5 alternatives to Surge AI | Prolific
results.content:
Note that Clickworker specializes in computer vision and conversational AI only. Clickworkers can tag or annotate text and images, analyze text, or verify AI output - but may not be able to support other kinds of projects.

Clickworker is an attractive Surge AI competitor for a few key reasons:

 Large workforce: With 6 million people in its crowd, Clickworker has one of the largest remote workforces available. This may make it faster to get the data you need.
 Specialization: The company’s focus on computer vision and conversational AI means its taskers are experienced in annotating these kinds of data.
 Support: Clickworker assigns a project manager to help you set up your dataset creation project.

When is Clickworker the best alternative to Surge AI? [...] When is Upwork the best alternative to Surge AI?

Choose Upwork when you want to work directly with labelers on your projects. Upwork is generally best suited to smaller, complex studies or tests—it’s not suitable for labeling massive datasets to train models on.

5. Encord

Encord is a software company that has created AI testing tools which researchers and AI companies can use themselves. Whether you want people to annotate images, test models, or label text, Encord gives you ‘plug and play’ tools to do just that. Once you’ve chosen the kind of labeling solution you want, you then invite people to do the labeling work.

Encord has a number of advantages over Surge AI: [...] Appen provides a number of AI training tools, including:

 Supervised fine-tuning
 Human preference ranking
 LLM evaluation
 A/B testing
 LLM red teaming
 Retrieval augmented generation

In addition to desk-based data annotation, Appen’s crowd can also support various other kinds of data generation. These include things like remote data collection (visiting places and taking photos, for instance), onsite collection (workers use equipment or carry out tasks at Appen’s own global facilities), and more.

Appen has a number of features that make it an appealing Surge AI alternative:
